rows.text: The Dolphins are 9-0 to the Over as a road underdog in division games over the last five seasons (+$818), going over the total by 10.4 PPG.
The Bills are 28-14 to the first-half Over at home over the last five seasons (+$1,260). That is the 2nd-best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
Josh Allen is 5-1 to the Over with Scott Novak officiating in his career (since 2019) (+$355), going over the total by 9.0 PPG.
Home teams with Scott Novak officiating are 46-58 straight up since 2020 (-$2,129).

Facts are facts. Dolphins are 6-1 ATS in their last seven games inside the AFC East and that's mainly because of inflated numbers.

Dolphins are 26-12-1 ATS against the AFC East since 2020 (+$1,170). That is the 3rd-best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
Josh Allen and the Bills have closed above a 14-pt favorite nine times as a duo, they are 8-1 SU and 3-5-1 ATS in those games, including 1-2-1 ATS when that game is in division.

Josh Allen has faced the Dolphins 17 times, he is 14-3 SU and 7-9-1 ATS, but as a big favorite he has come up short.

As a favorite of 6+ pts vs Miami, he is 7-1 SU but just 1-6-1 ATS, including 0-4-1 ATS as above a 7-pt favorite.

In the last 30 years, we've seen 34 teams close as a 16+ pt favorite inside the division -- those teams are 33-1 SU and 18-13-3 ATS in that span -- the one outright loss was the Patriots against the Dolphins in 2019.

Last week, Dolphins lost but covered, in Week 7 at Jets, Dolphins won outright and in Week 4 at the Vikings, Miami covered. The Dolphins haven't covered the spread in three straight road games in the same season since the end of 2022 (covered 5 straight road games).

Bills join an exclusive club. Not many teams have allowed 13 pts or less in 3 straight games while averaging 30+ PPG 10+ games into the season. Here is list since 1970 merger:

2026 Bills
2019 Ravens
2009 Vikings
2007 Patriots
1999 Rams
1987 49ers

Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).

rows.text: The Bears are 10-0-1 ATS in their 2nd straight home game over the last four seasons (+$922), covering by 9.8 PPG.
The Saints are 6-0 to the Under the week after a division game since the start of last season (+$545), going under the total by 4.2 PPG.
The Saints are 0-4 SU/ATS with Brad Rogers officiating over the last four seasons (-$400), failing to cover by 7.4 PPG.

In 43 career starts, Caleb Williams' biggest line as a favorite came in Week 15 last season vs. Browns as a 7.5-pt favorite. Caleb has closed above a 4-pt favorite six times and Chicago is just 2-4 ATS in those games.

+ Chicago hasn't closed as a favorite of 8 pts or more since 2020 -- Mitch Trubisky vs Mike Glennon.
+ Chicago hasn't closed as a double-digit favorite since 2018 -- Mitch Trubisky vs Nathan Peterman.

Bears haven't closed as a 9-pt favorite or higher at home in Chicago since October 10, 2013 against Eli Manning and the Giants. The Bears, Jets and Giants are the only three teams in the NFL without a home game as a 9+ pt favorite in this span before this week.

The Saints have been slow starters under Tyler Shough. They are 3-13-2 SU and 4-14 ATS in the first half with Shough at QB.

Saints are 1-8 against the first half spread this season, worst mark of any team in the NFL. Under Kellen Moore, Saints are 6-20 against the first half spread, also the work mark of any team since he was hired.

Ben Johnson is 19-9 SU and 18-9-1 ATS as coach of the Bears. On any extended prep time, his teams are 3-3 SU and 5-1 ATS -- this will be the first time his Bears are listed as a favorite on any extended prep time -- and looks like it will be a double-digit spread.
The line has been key to the Saints covering under Kellen Moore. As a favorite, or a dog of under 4 pts, New Orleans is 6-10 SU and 5-11 ATS. As a dog of 4+ pts, they are just 3-7 SU, but 7-3 ATS.
As a home favorite, Ben Johnson is 7-4 SU and ATS in the first quarter. In his last 7 games in this spot, he has outscored his opponents, 48-6.

Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).

rows.text:
Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).
Dak Prescott is 7-0 to the Over with Clete Blakeman officiating in his career (since 2016) (+$636), going over the total by 10.7 PPG.
Favorites with Clete Blakeman officiating are 82-105-4 ATS since 2015 (-$2,754).
The Cowboys haven’t done a good job at covering big numbers. As a favorite of 6+ pts, they’ve lost 6 in a row ATS, with their last cover coming at the end of the 2023 season.

In Dak Prescott's career, he has faced a non-divisional opponent at home as a favorite 41 times -- he is just 21-20 SU and 13-27-1  ATS. In his last 9 starts in this spot dating back to Week 13 of 2023, Dallas is 2-7 SU and 0-9 ATS, failing to cover by over 14 PPG.

98 QBs have faced 20+ non-divisional opponents at home, with your team listed as the favorite -- Dak's SU win pct is 3rd-worst and his ATS win pct is 4th-worst of the group in the Super Bowl era.

Keep fading? We've seen 197 coaches with 20+ games in Week 10 or later in the regular season -- Robert Saleh's 8-19 ATS (29.6%) mark is the 2nd-worst of any head coach (min. 20 gms). Saleh is 2-12 ATS in his last 14 games coached in this spot.
Since 2023, Dak Prescott and the Cowboys are 10-6 SU and 10-5-1 ATS vs the AFC and 16-20-1 SU and 13-24 ATS vs the NFC. Issues with their own.
Dak Prescott has started 43 career games where the total was above 50 — he is just 15-27-1 ATS in those games.

Cam Ward has started nine career games as above a one possession underdog (8.5 pts or more) -- Titans are 0-9 SU (5-4 ATS) in those games. The culprit? He's also 0-9 SU in the first half of those games, slow starters.

Brian Schottenheimer has coached 17 career games as a favorite with the Cowboys. Dallas is 7-10 SU and 4-12-1 ATS (25%) in those matchups.

Let's put that into perspective:
+ Six head coaches since the 1970 merger have started 4-12-1 ATS or worse through 17 games as a favorite.
+ Since 2000, that list is 4: Schotty, Dennis Allen, Kyle Shanahan and Jason Garrett (also a Cowboys head coach). Schotty's 7 wins as a favorite in first 17 games is tied for the fewest since 2000 as well.

Volatility usually isn't a good sign. Cowboys average 28+ PPG and allow 28+ PPG. Teams with those measurements cover just 46% of games over a 400+ game sample size. In Week 8 or later, those teams are 36-48-3 ATS (43%).
Feel the fade? In Week 10 or later, 43 teams have allowed 40+ pts in consecutive games. Those teams are 12-31 SU and 18-25 ATS, including 0-4 ATS over the last five seasons.
Since 2010, defenses that allowed 500+ total yards in their previous game, who are home favorites in their next game have struggled early on, going just 31-48 SU and 28-47-4 ATS in the first quarter.
The Cowboys are 8-2 ATS the week before Thanksgiving over the last 10 years, and they’ve covered by 12.6 points per game over the last five years.

rows.text:
Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).
The Buccaneers are 1-12 ATS with the Panthers on deck since 2020 (-$1,109), failing to cover by 9.2 PPG.
Home favorites with Adrian Hill officiating are 2-12 ATS since the start of last season (-$1,010), failing to cover by 4.0 PPG.
Games officiated by Adrian Hill are 15-8 to the Under since the start of last season (+$564).
Baker Mayfield and Jared Goff have faced off on opposite sidelines five times before this week -- Goff is 4-1 SU and ATS in those matchups, with the under also 4-1 in those games.

Buccaneers will be the first team to come into Detroit and face the Lions under Dan Campbell and Jared Goff off of a bye week. Of the six teams that have come into Detroit off any extended prep time to face Campbell & Goff, Detroit is still 5-1 SU and 4-2 ATS both full game and first half in those games.
After the trade deadline has come and gone, Dan Campbell's teams are 31-15-1 ATS (67%) in all their games in the second half of the season, the best of any coach with 30 or more games in that spot.
In tight spread games, Dan Campbell and Jared Goff have been tough to beat. With spread of 4 or less, they are 16-8 SU/ATS.
Teams coming off a blowout (20+ pts) in an International Series game have continued rolling, going 10-4 SU and 8-6 ATS, including 11-2-1 SU in the first half.

Lions have played 30 total games with Campbell and Goff at home where the total closed under 50 -- they are 20-10 SU/ATS in those games and 6-1 SU and 5-2 ATS when their opponent is allowing under 20 PPG on the season.

Lions coming back from an International Series games and Bucs off a bye -- we've seen that spot 14 times, with the team coming back overseas 5-8-1 SU/ATS and those teams are 5-9 1H ATS as well. Trend failed last week with the Steelers getting blown out by the Bengals.

Bengals pulled off a first last week. We've now seen five matchups where one team was coming off an International Series game on 7 days rest or less, face a team off a bye -- team off bye is now 4-1 SU and ATS after Cincinnati dismantled the Steelers.
Jared Goff is 4-0 SU in the Lions’ game before Thanksgiving, but 2-2 ATS. He’s 0-2 ATS when favored by 8 or more.

rows.text: The Chiefs are 32-10 to the Under at home over the last five seasons (+$1,909), going under the total by 4.6 PPG. That is the best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
The Chiefs are 16-4 to the Under with a total of 44 or lower over the last three seasons (+$1,055), going under the total by 5.5 PPG. That is the best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
The Chiefs are 10-2 to the Under with Brad Allen officiating since 2014 (+$709), going under the total by 10.0 PPG. That is the best mark of any team in the NFL since 2014.
Home favorites with Brad Allen officiating are 8-18 ATS over the last three seasons (-$1,065). Fits this week: Chiefs.

This will be Patrick Mahomes' 32nd career start as a double-digit favorite. He is 28-3 SU and 13-16-2 ATS in those games (14-17 1H ATS) -- since Tyreek Hill left, Mahomes and KC are 12-1 SU and 5-7-1 ATS in this spot.

Since start of last year, Mahomes has been DD fav twice -- winning 59-7 vs Commanders and Raiders.
Mahomes and Reid have faced four teams who have a first year head coach and QB, they have won those games by 10 PPG, winning on average 23.5 to 13.5, with the average line sitting at -11.5 range.
Different coach and QB, but Arizona has closed +13 or higher just four times since 2020 and they are not only 0-4 SU/ATS in those games, but they are losing those games by 22 PPG.

Never lost. Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes are 11-0 SU as a duo when facing a team who has scored 17 pts or less in consecutive games. Struggling on offense? Spags and this defense hasn't been the recipe.

Carson Beck made his first career start vs Super Bowl favorite Rams and now face the Chiefs -- tough beginnings. Since 1990, 3 other QBs have faced the pedigree (combined 22+ win total & ~23% preseason SB odds) of these teams in their first two starts:

2026 Carson Beck (ARI) vs LAR, KC
2022 Kenny Pickett (PIT) vs BUF, TB (only QB to get an outright win)
2011 Tyler Palko (KC) vs NE, PIT
1993 TJ Rubley (LAR) vs SF, SF

Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).

rows.text: The Eagles are 10-1 ATS at home against the Steelers in the Super Bowl era (+$821), covering by 9.0 PPG.
Home teams with Land Clark officiating are 19-37-1 ATS over the last four seasons (-$1,967), failing to cover by 4.6 PPG. Fits this week: Eagles, Steelers.
Mike McCarthy is 5-0 ATS with Land Clark officiating in his career (since 2020) (+$460), covering by 6.7 PPG.

Entering their bye last week, Eagles have lost 12 consecutive games against the 2nd half spread. Since 2005, that is tied for the longest 2H ATS losing streak for any team with ... the 2012-13 Eagles.

Eagles are not only 0-5 ATS at home this season, but they’ve lost 7 straight ATS at home dating back to last season. Their first 0-5 ATS start at home since 1983. The 7-game streak ties the 1983 team for the 2nd-longest in franchise history. The record is 10 (Oct 2012 – Oct 2013, Andy Reid into Chip Kelly).

Eagles are the 48th team in the Super Bowl era to start 0-5 ATS at home, and history says a bounce-back is more likely than not. The 47 teams before them went 74-52-2 ATS (58.7%) in their remaining home games that season.

Eagles haven't been their best at home in Philly as underdogs. They've lost 7 straight ATS (1-9 ATS in last ten) and they've lost 11 consecutive games outright as a home underdog -- their last outright win came in 2020 against Taysom Hill and the Saints.

Nick Sirianni is 0-10 SU (1-9 ATS) as a home underdog while with the Eagles -- the only head coach 0-10 SU or worse in this spot in the Super Bowl era.
A better spot than I expected. Steelers off road divisional game in primetime, playing on 7 days rest or less, those teams are actually 32-24 SU and 34-22 ATS in their next game since 2020.

Steelers are coming off a 20+ pt loss for the first time since Week 5 of 2023. Historically, Pittsburgh bounces back. How their best HC have performed in that spot:

Mike Tomlin: 12-2 ATS
Bill Cowher: 7-4-1 ATS
Chuck Noll: 21-9-2 ATS

Mike McCarthy in that spot: 9-15 SU, 9-13-2 ATS as a head coach.

After the Steelers score under 20 pts in their previous game with Aaron Rodgers, they are 6-0 SU and ATS, averaging 27.5 PPG in those matchups, covering the spread by over 10 PPG.

In Rodgers’ career, he is 36-19-2 ATS (65.5%) after his team scores under 20 pts in their previous game. In Super Bowl era, 66 QBs have had 50+ games in this spot, here is best ATS win pct:

1. Joe Montana: 39-14 ATS
2. Tom Brady: 46-24 ATS
3. Aaron Rodgers: 36-19-2 ATS

Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).

rows.text: The Panthers are 2-12 ATS as a home favorite since 2020 (-$955), failing to cover by 9.0 PPG. That is the worst mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
Bryce Young is 1-8 against the first-half spread against AFC opponents over the last three seasons (-$780).
The Ravens are 10-1 ATS in the middle of a road trip over the last five seasons (+$818), covering by 8.7 PPG.
Dave Canales is 16-5 to the Over at home in his career (since 2024) (+$955), going over the total by 6.6 PPG. That is the best mark of 31 head coaches with at least 10 such games since 2024.
Favorites with Shawn Hochuli officiating are 44-62-2 ATS since 2020 (-$2,119).
The Panthers are 10-2 to the Under with a total of 44 or lower since the start of last season (+$709), going under the total by 5.6 PPG. That is the best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.

Bryce Young has started 12 career home games with a tight spread (4 or less), Panthers are 5-7 SU and 6-5-1 ATS in those games, but Carolina is 0-3 SU/ATS this season, losing to the Broncos, Bucs and Bears.

Dave Canales is 18-8 ATS off of a SU loss as coach of the Panthers and 17-5 ATS with Bryce Young at QB.

That duo is 4-9 SU and 5-8 ATS off of a SU win.
Not a good sign. Panthers had 17 penalties in the win last week. Teams with more than 15 penalties in their previous game are just 16-20 SU and 12-21-3 ATS in their next game dating back to 2000.
Through Week 10, the NFC South is 4-17 at home (.190), the worst division home record through Week 10 since the NFL’s modern divisions were established in 1970.

Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).

rows.text: Favorites with Alex Kemp officiating are 31-11 ATS over the last three seasons (+$1,738), covering by 6.2 PPG. Fits this week: Chargers, Jets.

Jets are 2-8 ATS the week after facing Josh Allen since 2020 (-$616), failing to cover by 6.2 PPG.

Dating back to 2012, Jets are 1-21 SU and 3-18-1 ATS the week after facing the Bills, failing to cover by 7.6 PPG.
Games officiated by Alex Kemp are 17-8 to the Under since the start of last season (+$745), going under the total by 4.5 PPG.

Jets play their first road game on the west coast under Aaron Glenn this week. New York's last game in this spot came in Week 1 of 2024 with Aaron Rodgers. Since 2000, Jets are 9-18 SU and 9-16-2 ATS in this spot.
Jim Harbaugh has coached 18 total games where his team was on short rest -- they are 12-6 SU and 11-7 ATS, including 6-2 ATS with the Chargers.

There are depressing stats, but the Jets being terrible even in a good spot after getting blown out is very Jets.

New York is 3-15 SU and 4-14 ATS off a loss by 14+ points in their last 18 games in that spot dating back to 2022, failing to cover by 5.7 PPG.
Maybe the easiest point to Aaron Glenn's struggles: the Jets have played four games where Glenn and New York had a rest advantage, they are 0-4 SU, averaging just 15.2 PPG in those matchups.

Jets have lost 5 straight games outright and now start a road trip in the Chargers and then the Dolphins. Teams in that first game of road trip, on a 5+ game SU losing streak are 90-67-1 ATS (57%) in the Super Bowl era.
Chargers are 0-4 ATS at home this season and have lost 5 straight ATS at home dating back to last season.

At home in L.A., Justin Herbert is 14-6 SU and 12-8 ATS when facing teams below .500 SU. In Week 9, Chargers lost to the Texans who were below .500 — that broke a 10-game win streak for Herbert, Chargers at home in this spot dating back to 2021.

Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).

rows.text: The Raiders are 14-4 ATS against the Broncos over the last decade (+$889), covering by 5.4 PPG.
The Raiders are 0-4 ATS on the road with Craig Wrolstad officiating since 2020 (-$400), failing to cover by 14.8 PPG.
Sean Payton is 15-3 straight up with a rest advantage of 3+ days since 2015 (+$857). That is the best mark of 24 head coaches with at least 10 such games in that span.
Sean Payton has had success vs inexperienced QBs. He is 30-8 SU and 22-16 ATS when facing QBs within their first 5 career starts. With Bo Nix and Drew Brees, Payton is 25-5 SU in these spots.
Undefeated. Bo NIx is 15-0 SU and 8-7 ATS as a favorite of 4 pts or more and he is 13-0 SU and 6-7 ATS as a favorite of 6+ points.

Since the merger, having experience starting in Denver has mattered. QBs in their first start in Denver have won just 28.6% of games outright, covering 44.8%. QBs with experience in Denver are 34.7% SU and 48.1% ATS -- a 6% jump SU and a 3%+ jump ATS.

First-year starting QBs, making their first start in Denver, 9-36 SU and 17-26-2 ATS.
Raiders haven't beaten a team outright who was over .500 SU since the end of 2023 (Christmas Day vs Chiefs) -- Raiders have lost 18 consecutive games in this spot, going 9-9 ATS in those games.

Broncos have been dominant at home in Denver.

+ They've covered 7 straight home games -- their longest home ATS win streak since 1992 (also 7 games). 
+ Broncos haven't covered 8 straight home games since 1978.

In their last 20 home games, Denver is 18-2 SU and 16-4 ATS.

Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).

rows.text: The Giants are 7-0 straight up against the AFC South over the last five seasons (+$1,197).
Trevor Lawrence is 5-18 against the first-half spread against NFC opponents in his career (since 2021) (-$1,480). That is the worst mark of 51 QBs with at least 10 such games since 2021.
Home underdogs with Carl Cheffers officiating are 22-12-3 ATS since 2020 (+$816). Fits this week: Giants.
John Harbaugh is 28-9 straight up with a rest advantage of 3+ days in his career (since 2008) (+$436). That is the 3rd-best mark of 38 head coaches with at least 10 such games since 2008.
Any NFC opponent hasn't been the easiest for Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars. Jacksonville is 7-16 SU and 8-15 ATS vs. NFC with Lawrence, including 4-3 SU and 3-4 ATS as favorites.
As an underdog with a backup QB since 2013, John Harbaugh is 18-7 ATS, including 3-1 ATS with the Giants.
On extended prep time (more than a full week, 7 days) and off a loss, John Harbaugh has been excellent. He is 16-5 SU/ATS as a head coach, including 3-0 ATS as underdogs in this spot.

Since the beginning of last season, Trevor Lawrence is 12-3 ATS as a favorite during the regular season, covering the spread by 9.6 PPG.

In their last 18 games overall, Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars are 14-4 ATS, covering the spread by over 10.9 PPG in that span.
A weird schedule quirk. Jaguars could become 19th team in Super Bowl era to be favored by 6+ pts in three straight road games and first since Cowboys in 2021.
Under Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence, Jaguars have played 7 games on a road trip (2nd game or later road or neutral), they are 5-2 SU in those games -- 0-2 SU vs Texans and 5-0 SU vs all other teams.

Liam Coen is now 18-9 ATS -- his teams are covering the spread by 6.9 PPG -- that is the highest cover margin for any head coach thru 27 games in the Super Bowl era. 2nd on that list behind Coen? John Harbaugh in his first 27 games with the Ravens, where he went 19-8 ATS, covering by 6.2 PPG.

Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).

rows.text: The 49ers are 1-8 ATS against the NFC North over the last five seasons (-$709), failing to cover by 5.8 PPG.
Kevin O'Connell and Kirk Cousins as a QB-coach duo are 8-1 to the Under together over the last four seasons (+$627), going under the total by 4.4 PPG.

This will be the 30th International game (series and overall) played outside the morning window (1p ET or later). Favorites are 22-7 SU and 19-9-1 ATS in those games, covering the spread by almost 6 PPG.

Kevin O'Connell and Kirk Cousins have a small edge in International Series game experience compared to Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy, playing 5 and 3 respectively. We've seen 17 games where both coach and QB have an experience edge, they are 9-8 SU and 11-6 ATS.

The markets caught Minnesota at just the right time. Vikings were 6-0 SU and then they started a 4-game stretch, all as underdogs. No team that started 5-0 SU or better had then been an underdog in each of the next four games -- until now.

+ Only two other teams have started 5-0 SU or better and been underdogs in 4 straight games at any point that season: 2009 Broncos, 2015 Falcons.
+ The Vikings’ 2024 run (5-0 start, then three straight games as underdogs) was the closest any team had come to that until now.

Just need some offense. Dating back to 2024, in the Vikings last 21 games where they score 20 pts or more, they are 19-2 SU and 17-3-1 ATS -- that includes 17-0 SU with Cousins, Kyler, JJ, Brosmer and Darnold and 2-2 SU with Carson Wentz.
All KOC needs is some consistency. When the Vikings don’t lose the turnover margin under O’Connell they are 42-6 SU (88%).
The 49ers are 13-2 to the first-half Over away from home since the start of last season -- going over the first half total by 4.4 PPG.

Vikings have another "Game of the Year." In Week 9, Vikings faced the Bills. In Week 11, Vikings face the 49ers.

+ In a team's 8th game or later, 2026 will be the first year since 2000 to have 2+ games where an offense scoring 30+ PPG faced a defense allowing 14 PPG or less.
+ 2026 Vikings will be first team since 1968 Chiefs to have 2+ matchups, 8+ games in with that defense facing that high-powered an offense.

Defenses in these matchups are 9-14 SU and 10-12-1 ATS.

In Brock Purdy's career as a starter, he has faced a defense allowing 17 PPG or less, eight times -- San Francisco is 2-6 SU and 1-7 ATS in those eight games. 49ers have lost six straight games outright in this spot.
In the Vikings last nine games away from home, the under is 8-1, going under the total by 9.7 PPG — the only over in that span? A game last season vs Cowboys.

Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills

rows.text: The Bengals are 13-1 ATS at a rest disadvantage of 3+ days since 2020 (+$1,090), covering by 4.9 PPG. That is the best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
Joe Burrow is 13-3-1 ATS against NFC opponents over the last five seasons (+$878), covering by 3.8 PPG. That is the best mark of 43 QBs with at least 10 such games in that span.
The Commanders are 7-1 to the Over with Bill Vinovich officiating since 2020 (+$536), going over the total by 8.3 PPG.
Home teams with Bill Vinovich officiating are 62-92-2 ATS over the last decade (-$3,483).

What a massive win for the Commanders last week, beating the Giants on the road on Thursday Night Football. 

The last time the Commanders won or covered the spread off a SU win was back in the Divisional Round of the playoffs in 2024 — they are 0-7 SU/ATS after a SU win since, losing outright by 12 PPG.

At 32-15-1 ATS (68%) on the road, Joe Burrow has the 2nd-highest ATS win pct for any QB in the Super Bowl era behind just Teddy Bridgewater.

136 QBs have made 40+ road starts in the Super Bowl era. Here are the QBs with 60%+ ATS win pct and 55%+ SU win pct: Joe Burrow, Joe Montana, Jim McMahon, Lamar Jackson and Donovan McNabb.

The defense has held opponents back this year. Bengals have now won 8 straight games outright when scoring 28+ points and they are 12-1 SU (11-1-1 ATS) when scoring 28+ points in their last 13 games in that spot.
Joe Burrow is 0-2 SU/ATS in his career vs. Commanders. Burrow is only 0-3 SU/ATS vs. one other franchise and that's the Chargers.
Last 20 yrs, we've seen 40 home underdogs of 6+ pts on MNF -- they are 9-31 SU and 23-17 ATS, including 24-16 against the first half spread.

Joe Burrow is -115 to win the NFL MVP award entering Week 11. In the last 5 years, only one other QB has been the odds-on favorite to win the award in the first 11 weeks of the season: Josh Allen in Week 5 last year at -105.

Cardinals and Dolphins have both dropped two straight and look to get right vs. KC and Buffalo. When your team is on a losing streak (2+ games), here are the last QBs you want to see...

Best moneyline win pct when opp. is on 2+ game SU losing streak since 1990 (min 15 starts):
1. Patrick Mahomes: 27-2 SU (93%)
2. Tom Brady: 68-10 SU (88%)
3. Josh Allen: 33-6 SU (85%)
This season, the NFC South is 8-19 SU and 9-18 ATS playing teams outside their division -- that ATS mark is by far the worst mark in the NFL.

In Week 11, we might have 5 double-digit favorites:

Colts at Texans
Saints at Bears
Cardinals at Chiefs
Dolphins at Bills
Raiders at Broncos

+ Most games w/ DD spread in first 11 weeks of a season since 2009 (most before Week 13 since 2010).
+ We could close with 9 of 13 games (69.2%) at a spread of 6+. That share has been matched or beaten in Weeks 1–11 only three times since 2010: 2020 Week 5 (10 of 14) and 2014 Week 10 and 2013 Week 8 (9 of 13).

Two for the money? Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck are onto start No. 2 after both teams scored under 2 TDs at 13 pts or less. Last 20 yrs, we've seen 56 QBs in their second start after their team scored 13 pts or less in their last game -- they are 33-22-1 ATS (60%).
This season, road division underdogs are 11-15-1 SU (42.6%) and 16-11 ATS. The straight up ROI for those road div. dogs is over 31% through ten weeks. The 4th-best SU start in the last 40 years.

The NFL has 32 teams. 9 of them have a head coach who has a defensive background -- Glenn, Quinn, DeMeco, Hafley, Minter, Macdonald, Vrabel, Saleh, Bowles. They are a combined 26-40-3 ATS (39%) when facing a non-defensive HC.

These teams have finished .500 ATS or worse in 9 of 10 weeks this season.

Win total analysis entering Week 10.

Settled
Over: CLE | Under: PHI, LAC, BAL

Up Next
HOU under w/ loss
ARI over w/ win
Both James Cook and Christian McCaffrey have scored a TD in 8 consecutive games entering Week 11, the longest active streaks in the NFL.

Week 11’s 13 games average 8.23 points per spread, the highest for any week in the first 11 weeks of a season since 1977, not counting the 1987 Week 5 strike-replacement week.

Since 2010, only 2 of 287 weeks averaged more. Since 2020, only 1 of 117 (2021 Week 17).

Teams to score 3+ TDs (pass + rush + def.) are just 92-50-5 ATS (64.8%) through 10 weeks this season, the lowest ATS win pct for teams in this spot since 1990. The gap between lowest and 2nd-lowest is 2.5%, with 2nd-lowest coming in 2020.

Favorites have had a great start to the season, but almost all of that damage has come on the road.

Road favorites are 36-21-2 ATS (63.2) this season — the best start thru 10 weeks for road favs since 1972. Over the last two weeks, road favs are 15-1 SU and 14-1-1 ATS.

Home favorites are just 36-45-2 ATS (44%).

Home teams are 69-72-1 SU (48.9%) in the NFL this season through ten weeks. For the 2nd time in the last 40 years, home teams are under .500 SU at this mark in the season (2021).

The issue has been low favorite or underdog home teams. Teams who close as a dog or favorite of under 6 pts are just 45-62-1 SU (42.1%).
